{{center block/s}}</noinclude><section begin="ode10" />By the Făng-water grows the white millet<ref>'The [[w:Panicum miliaceum|white millet]],' a valuable species, grown near the [[w:zh:灃河 (渭河)|Făng]], suggests to the writer the idea of all the men of ability whom [[w:King Wu of Zhou|Wû]] collected around him.</ref>;—{{lb}}Did
not king Wû show wisdom in his employment of officers?{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He would leave his plans to his descendants,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And secure comfort and support to his son.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was king Wû!
{{center block/e}}
<section end="ode10" />

{{c|The Second Decade, or that of {{tooltip|Shăng Min|Shēng Mín}}.}}

{{c|{{sc|Ode 1. The Shăng Min.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|The legend of Hâu-''k''î:—his conception; his birth; the perils of his infancy; his boyish habits of agriculture; his subsequent methods and teaching of agriculture; his founding of certain sacrifices; and the honours of sacrifice paid to him by the house of ''K''âu.}}

Of [[w:Hou Ji|Hâu-''k''î]] there is some notice on the [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/Odes of the Temple and the Altar/The Sacrificial Odes of Kâu/Decade 1/Ode 10|tenth ode of the first decade of the Sacrificial Odes of ''K''âu]]. To him the [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|kings of ''K''âu]] traced their lineage. Of [[w:Jiang Yuan|''K''iang Yüan]], his mother, our knowledge is very scanty. It is said that she was a daughter of the House of [[w:Tai (city)|Thâi]], which traced its lineage up to [[w:Shennong|Shăn-nung]] in prehistoric times. From the first stanza of this piece it appears that she was married, and had been so for some time without having any child. But who her husband was it is impossible to say with certainty. As the ''K''âu surname was [[w:Ji (Zhou dynasty ancestral surname)|''K''î]], he must have been one of the descendants of [[w:Yellow Emperor|Hwang Tî]].
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
The first birth of (our) people<ref>Our 'people' is of course the people of [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|''K''âu]]. The whole piece is about the individual from whom the House of ''K''âu sprang, of which were the kings of the dynasty so called.</ref>{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Was from {{tooltip|''K''iang Yüan|Jiāng Yuán}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
How did she give birth to (our) people?{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
She had presented a pure offering and sacrificed<ref>To whom [[w:Jiang Yuan|''K''iang Yüan]] sacrificed and prayed we are not told, but I receive the impression that it was to God,—see the next stanza,—and that she did so all alone with the special object which is mentioned.</ref>,{{lb}}
